hypothesis: Ensemble two structurally different past candidates in one run_model() call: (1) the plain single-task BPR-FM (current best mechanism) trained with the video `tag` field added to the feature set (per iter 6's feature_addition finding, +0.0001 alone), and (2) the multi-task FM_MT with the auxiliary is_like head (per iter 14's multi_task finding, alpha_aux=0.03, +0.0004 alone) trained on the same tag-augmented fields — then average their z-scored prediction scores. Since one model's edge comes from extra input signal (tag) and the other's comes from an auxiliary supervision gradient, their errors should be less correlated than iter 17's same-mechanism pairing, giving averaging a better chance to cross the acceptance margin.
reflection: Iter 17's ensemble of plain BPR-FM + FM_MT barely moved GAUC and didn't move nDCG@5 at all — expected, since both models shared the exact same input features and interaction structure, differing only by one small auxiliary loss term, so their errors were highly correlated. The two individually-above-baseline candidates that are NOT both from the same mechanism are iter 14 (multi_task: auxiliary is_like head) and iter 6 (feature_addition: video `tag` field) — these differ in lever category (loss/architecture vs. input features), so their errors are more likely genuinely decorrelated.
expected_effect: GAUC should move more than nDCG@5, since averaging two models whose errors stem from genuinely different sources (feature vs. loss) primarily smooths per-user pairwise-ranking noise across the full candidate set, which is what GAUC directly aggregates, while nDCG@5's top-5 cutoff remains sensitive to whichever single model ranks the very top items and is less responsive to averaging.
